decisions.reason: Removing the print-version deliverable does not remove or alter the magazine layout and Flat Plan arrangement required for the digital output.
The article-end whitespace requirement applies to the magazine layout generally and remains necessary for the digital flipbook.
Article image remediation is not specific to the print version and remains applicable to the digital magazine.
Advertisement sharpness remains a requirement for the digital magazine PDF and is not contingent on producing a print version.
The source removes only the print version; the separate digital flipbook deliverable remains active unchanged.
The polished, brand-aligned visual style remains applicable to the digital magazine independently of the removed print output.
The required source of magazine articles is independent of whether a print-ready version is delivered.
Including the cover-listed articles remains necessary for content consistency in the digital magazine.
Readable article typography remains required for the digital magazine and is not print-specific.
Future word-count guidance addresses layout whitespace in later issues and is not logically changed by removal of the current print deliverable.
The color-usage rule applies to magazine presentation and remains valid for the digital version.
Author names, photographs, sizing, sourcing, and placement remain required on digital article pages independently of print output.
